newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek M3 rises provisionally 12.4pct yr/yr in Feb.
newsitem.headline: Greek M3 rises provisionally 12.4pct yr/yr in Feb.

text.p: Greek M3 money supply grew provisionally 12.4 percent year-on-year in February from a revised 13.6 percent in January, overshooting the central bank's 6.0-9.0 percent target range for end-97, the Bank of Greece said.

"This development in M3 relates to interest and principle payments abroad which resulted in a reduction of forex reserves by $805 million in February against an increase of $1.293 billion in January," it said in a statement.
M4 money supply grew provisionally 7.8 percent year-on-year in February from a revised 11.5 percent in January.
"The greater deceleration in the growth of M4 compared to M3 in February reflects the further decrease of placements in T-bills by individuals," it said.
Placements by individuals in short-term securities fell by 1.379 billion in the first two months of 1997 against an increase of 66 billion in the same period in 1996, it said.
